## Approach

Collinearity is checked within three groups of candidate predictors:
topography, fire weather, and vegetation. For each group we report:

- pairwise Spearman correlations (rank-based, robust to the skewed and
  bounded distributions of many predictors);
- variance inflation factors (VIF), which capture multicollinearity among
  more than two variables at once. VIF > 5 is flagged, VIF > 10 is
  severe.

Pixel-level checks use one random sample of pixels, which keeps the
computations fast with little loss of precision. Fire weather is constant
within each fire, so it is checked at the fire level instead (one row per
fire); pixel-level correlations would weight fires by their size.

```{r helpers, include = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
#' Variance inflation factors for a set of numeric columns
#'
#' Regresses each column on all others and returns `1 / (1 - R^2)`.
#' Aliased columns (perfectly collinear) return `Inf`.
#'
#' @param DT `data.table` or `data.frame` of numeric predictors.
#'
#' @return named numeric vector of VIFs, sorted decreasingly.
#' @keywords internal
calcVIF <- function(DT) {
  DT <- as.data.frame(DT)
  vifs <- vapply(names(DT), function(v) {
    fit <- lm(reformulate(paste0("`", setdiff(names(DT), v), "`"), paste0("`", v, "`")),
              data = DT)
    r2 <- summary(fit)$r.squared
    if (r2 >= 1 - 1e-10) Inf else 1 / (1 - r2)
  }, numeric(1))
  sort(round(vifs, 2), decreasing = TRUE)
}

#' Spearman correlation heatmap
#'
#' @param DT `data.table` or `data.frame` of numeric predictors.
#' @param title character. Plot title.
#'
#' @return a `ggplot` object (lower triangle, with coefficients printed).
#' @keywords internal
plotCorr <- function(DT, title = NULL) {
  ## matrix must not be called `rho`: inside DT[...] that name refers to the column
  rhoMat <- cor(DT, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  rhoMat[upper.tri(rhoMat)] <- NA
  rhoDT <- as.data.table(as.table(rhoMat))[!is.na(N)]
  setnames(rhoDT, c("var1", "var2", "rho"))
  rhoDT[, `:=`(var1 = factor(var1, levels = colnames(rhoMat)),
               var2 = factor(var2, levels = rev(colnames(rhoMat))))]
  ggplot(rhoDT, aes(var1, var2, fill = rho)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", rho)), size = 2.8) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Spearman\nrho", title = title) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

#' Pairs with |rho| above a threshold
#'
#' @param DT `data.table` or `data.frame` of numeric predictors.
#' @param thresh numeric. Absolute Spearman correlation threshold.
#'
#' @return `data.table` of variable pairs and their correlation, sorted by
#'   decreasing |rho|.
#' @keywords internal
highCorrPairs <- function(DT, thresh = 0.7) {
  rho <- cor(DT, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  rho[upper.tri(rho, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
  out <- as.data.table(as.table(rho))[!is.na(N) & abs(N) >= thresh]
  setnames(out, c("var1", "var2", "rho"))
  out[, rho := round(rho, 3)]
  ## `[]` so the result prints (`:=` returns invisibly)
  out[order(-abs(rho))][]
}
```

```{r sample, cache = FALSE}
set.seed(5813)
sampDT <- summaryABSK_AllData[sample(.N, min(.N, 2e5))]
```

## Topographic variables

`Aspect` uses the code `-117` for flat pixels (`r round(100 * summaryABSK_AllData[, mean(Aspect == -117)], 1)`% of pixels),
so it is set to `NA` here. Its circular scale makes linear correlations
meaningless anyway; `SCOS`/`SSIN` (slope × cos/sin of aspect) are the
linear alternatives.

```{r topoVars, cache = FALSE}
topoVars <- c("Elevation", "PctSlope", "DegSlope", "SurfAspectRatio",
              "SCOS", "SSIN", "TRASP", "Aspect",
              "CTI", "Curv", "SlopePosition", "SurfReliefRatio")
topoDT <- sampDT[, ..topoVars]
topoDT[Aspect == -117, Aspect := NA]
```

```{r topoCorr, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
plotCorr(topoDT, "Topographic variables (all)")
highCorrPairs(topoDT)
```

`SurfAspectRatio` is an exact function of slope (constant multiple of
sec(slope)); `DegSlope` is a monotonic transform of `PctSlope`:

```{r topoSAR}
topoDT[, .(SurfAspectRatio_over_secSlope = range(SurfAspectRatio / (1 / cos(DegSlope * pi / 180))))]
```

VIFs for the full set and for the candidate set (dropping redundant or
circular variables):

```{r topoVIF}
calcVIF(topoDT[, !c("Aspect", "DegSlope", "SurfAspectRatio")])

topoCand <- c("Elevation", "PctSlope", "SCOS", "SSIN", "CTI", "SurfReliefRatio")
calcVIF(topoDT[, ..topoCand])
```

## Fire-weather variables

Weather summaries (first three days of each fire) take a single value per
fire, so correlations are computed across fires.

```{r weatherVars, cache = FALSE}
weatherVars <- grep("^(mean|min|max|cv|range)(Temp|RH|WS|Rain|FFMC|DMC|DC|ISI|BUI|FWI)$|^startJulDay$",
                    names(summaryABSK_AllData), value = TRUE)

## confirm weather is constant within fires
stopifnot(summaryABSK_AllData[, lapply(.SD, uniqueN), by = FIRE_NAME,
                              .SDcols = weatherVars][, all(unlist(.SD) == 1), .SDcols = weatherVars])

weatherDT <- unique(summaryABSK_AllData[, c("FIRE_NAME", weatherVars), with = FALSE])
nrow(weatherDT)

## drop near-constant variables
weatherDT[, lapply(.SD, uniqueN), .SDcols = weatherVars]
```

With `r nrow(weatherDT)` fires and `r length(weatherVars)` weather
variables, VIFs for the full set cannot be computed (more variables than
fires); correlations are the main diagnostic here.

```{r weatherCorr, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 13}
weatherNum <- weatherDT[, ..weatherVars]
## minRain is almost always 0; cvRain has NAs where mean rain is 0
weatherNum <- weatherNum[, !c("minRain", "cvRain")]
plotCorr(weatherNum, "Fire-weather variables (one row per fire)")
highCorrPairs(weatherNum, thresh = 0.8)
```

Within each weather variable, `mean`, `min`, `max` and `range` are expected to
be strongly related; across variables, the FWI-system indices are built from
one another (e.g. BUI from DMC and DC; FWI from ISI and BUI).

```{r weatherMeanVIF}
## VIF among the mean values only
meanVars <- grep("^mean", names(weatherNum), value = TRUE)
calcVIF(weatherNum[, ..meanVars])
```

## Vegetation variables

The species-group percentages (`FlamConif`, `Abie`, `Lari`, `Decid`) are a
composition: they sum to 100 on forested pixels and to 0 on non-forested
pixels (where forest attributes are filled with 0):

```{r vegComposition}
sampDT[, .(n = .N,
           pctSum100 = mean(FlamConif + Abie + Lari + Decid == 100),
           pctSum0 = mean(FlamConif + Abie + Lari + Decid == 0)),
       by = isForest]
```

This closure makes the four groups, plus `isForest`, linearly dependent: any
one can be computed from the others. Including all of them inflates VIFs
regardless of the ecological relationships between them.

```{r vegVars, cache = FALSE}
vegVars <- c("FlamConif", "Abie", "Lari", "Decid",
             "HEIGHT_LOWER", "HEIGHT_UPPER", "CROWN_CLOSURE_LOWER", "STAND_AGE",
             "UNDERSTOREY", "isForest", "SMR_ord", "SMR_wet")
vegDT <- sampDT[, ..vegVars][, lapply(.SD, as.numeric)]
```

```{r vegCorr, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
plotCorr(vegDT, "Vegetation variables (all pixels)")
highCorrPairs(vegDT)
```

Forest attributes are 0 on non-forested pixels, so correlations over all
pixels partly reflect the forest/non-forest split. Restricting to forested
pixels shows the relationships within forests:

```{r vegCorrForest, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
vegForestDT <- vegDT[isForest == 1, !"isForest"]
plotCorr(vegForestDT, "Vegetation variables (forested pixels only)")
highCorrPairs(vegForestDT)
```

VIFs for the candidate set used in model selection, and with one
composition group dropped (here `FlamConif`, the reference group, which is
present on almost all forested pixels):

```{r vegVIF}
vegCand <- c("FlamConif", "Abie", "Lari", "Decid", "HEIGHT_LOWER",
             "UNDERSTOREY", "isForest", "SMR_wet")
calcVIF(na.omit(vegDT[, ..vegCand]))

calcVIF(na.omit(vegDT[, setdiff(vegCand, "FlamConif"), with = FALSE]))
```

## Non-collinear variable lists

Selection rule, applied within each group:

1. Remove structural redundancies by hand (exact transforms, duplicates,
   circular variables, compositional closure), as shown above.
2. Among the remaining pool, drop variables with pairwise
   |Spearman ρ| ≥ 0.7, using `caret::findCorrelation()` (exact = TRUE),
   which, for each correlated pair, removes the variable with the larger
   mean absolute correlation with all others.
3. Iteratively drop the variable with the highest VIF until all VIFs are < 5.

Pools are the candidate predictors used for model selection in
`DAfires_sevModelsGAMLSS_ngbAvg.Rmd`. Categorical candidates (`LandCover`,
`DIST1`) are not covered by these numeric checks; they are listed
separately. Note that `isForest` is a collapse of `LandCover`
(`PF` vs the rest), so the two should not enter the same model.

```{r selectVars, cache = FALSE}
#' Select a non-collinear subset of numeric predictors
#'
#' Drops variables with pairwise |Spearman rho| >= `cutoff`
#' (`caret::findCorrelation`, exact = TRUE), then iteratively drops the
#' variable with the highest VIF until all VIFs are < `maxVIF`.
#'
#' @param DT `data.table` of numeric predictors (no NAs for the VIF step).
#' @param cutoff numeric. Absolute Spearman correlation threshold.
#' @param maxVIF numeric. Maximum VIF allowed in the retained set.
#'
#' @return character vector of retained column names.
#' @keywords internal
selectNonCollinear <- function(DT, cutoff = 0.7, maxVIF = 5) {
  drop <- caret::findCorrelation(cor(DT, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
                                 cutoff = cutoff, names = TRUE, exact = TRUE)
  keep <- setdiff(names(DT), drop)
  vifs <- calcVIF(DT[, ..keep])
  while (length(keep) > 2 && max(vifs) >= maxVIF) {
    message("Dropping ", names(vifs)[1], " (VIF = ", vifs[1], ")")
    keep <- setdiff(keep, names(vifs)[1])
    vifs <- calcVIF(DT[, ..keep])
  }
  keep
}

## topography: DegSlope, SurfAspectRatio (≡ slope), Aspect (circular, flat code),
## TRASP (aspect transform), Curv/SlopePosition (not candidates) excluded by hand
topoPool <- c("Elevation", "PctSlope", "SCOS", "SSIN", "CTI", "SurfReliefRatio")
topoKeep <- selectNonCollinear(topoDT[, ..topoPool])

## vegetation: FlamConif dropped as the reference composition group (closure);
## HEIGHT_UPPER (≡ HEIGHT_LOWER) excluded by hand
vegPool <- c("Abie", "Lari", "Decid", "HEIGHT_LOWER", "UNDERSTOREY",
             "isForest", "SMR_ord", "SMR_wet")
vegKeep <- selectNonCollinear(na.omit(vegDT[, ..vegPool]))

## climate (fire weather): FWI-system indices summarised over the first 3 days,
## at fire level. range* excluded (range = max - min).
climPool <- grep("^(mean|min|max|cv)(FFMC|DMC|DC|ISI|BUI|FWI)$", names(weatherDT), value = TRUE)
climKeep <- selectNonCollinear(weatherDT[, ..climPool])

list(topographic = topoKeep, vegetation = vegKeep, climate = climKeep)
```

VIFs of the retained sets:

```{r selectVIF}
calcVIF(topoDT[, ..topoKeep])
calcVIF(na.omit(vegDT[, ..vegKeep]))
calcVIF(weatherDT[, ..climKeep])
```

```{r exportVars, cache = FALSE}
nonCollinearVars <- list(
  topographic = topoKeep,
  vegetation = vegKeep,
  climate = climKeep,
  categorical = c("LandCover", "DIST1"),
  meta = list(
    created = Sys.time(),
    source = "analyses/DAfires_collinearityCheck.Rmd",
    dataCacheId = "185c1b8db3c9788d",
    rule = "hand-removed structural redundancies; then |Spearman rho| >= 0.7 via caret::findCorrelation(exact = TRUE); then iterative removal of the highest VIF until all VIF < 5",
    sample = "topography/vegetation: 2e5 random pixels (seed 5813); climate: one row per fire",
    nFires = nrow(weatherDT)
  )
)
outDir <- "analyses/outputs"
dir.create(outDir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(nonCollinearVars, file.path(outDir, "nonCollinearVars.rds"))
```

The lists are saved to `analyses/outputs/nonCollinearVars.rds`.
